verdict.rationale: LangGraph is a code-first framework. Its core capabilities are documented as programmatic APIs: graph construction, checkpointing, state inspection and modification, interrupts resumed via Command, and stream/astream modes. The local Agent Server also 'exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc.', so most functionality is reachable without a UI. However, no evidence explicitly states parity between the API and any UI (e.g., the LangSmith visualization and debugging tooling), and the probe found no published OpenAPI spec on the docs domain. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity statement, a published OpenAPI spec for the Agent Server, and independent hands-on corroboration that UI-only features are absent.
